- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the latter half of the forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially during sharp upward trends.
- Overreacts to short-term volatility, overshooting peaks and failing to capture sustained upward trends.
- Shows mean reversion bias: forecasts often revert to historical averages too quickly, missing prolonged upward momentum.
- When true prices rise sharply, model fails to anticipate the full magnitude of the spike, underestimating the peak.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the final 5–10 days, failing to capture late-stage price acceleration.
- Model exhibits “early correction” bias: overcorrects downward after a spike, missing the continuation of upward trend.
